_comment: Dictyostelium glossary for the Education hub. Edit to add terms.

terms.def: The stage where starving amoebae move together (chemotax) toward cAMP signaling centers to form a multicellular mound.
The state cells reach a few hours into starvation when they can both relay and respond to cAMP and begin streaming.
The ability of cells to distinguish self/kin from non-self during aggregation, governed by the tgrB1/tgrC1 genes.
The single-celled, free-living feeding form of Dictyostelium that grows by engulfing bacteria.
Prestalk-type cells scattered in the prespore region of the slug; they contribute to structures during culmination.
A lab strain (e.g. AX2, AX3, AX4) that can grow in liquid nutrient medium without bacteria, enabling large-scale culture.
The pulsatile circuit in which a cAMP signal triggers cells to synthesize and secrete more cAMP, propagating waves that organize aggregation.
Directed cell movement up a chemical gradient; in Dictyostelium classically toward cAMP (aggregation) or folate (feeding).
The final morphogenetic stage in which the slug stands up and forms a fruiting body (stalk + spore mass).
Differentiation-Inducing Factor 1, a chlorinated polyketide morphogen that promotes prestalk/stalk cell fate.
The terminal structure: a cellular stalk holding aloft a sorus (ball of spores) on a basal disc.
The hemispherical aggregate of ~10^5 cells formed at the end of aggregation, where cell-type differentiation begins.
Engulfment of particles (bacteria) by amoebae; the basis of Dictyostelium's use as a model for host-pathogen and immune cell biology.
Cells in the posterior of the slug fated to become spores; marked by genes such as pspA, cotB, and cotC.
Cells in the anterior of the slug fated to become the stalk; marked by genes such as ecmA and ecmB.
The migrating, sausage-shaped multicellular stage with established anterior-posterior cell-type pattern.
Restriction Enzyme-Mediated Integration, a classic insertional mutagenesis method for tagging and disrupting Dictyostelium genes.
An amoeba that switches from a unicellular to a cooperative multicellular lifestyle under stress — Dictyostelium's defining trait.
The spherical spore mass at the top of the fruiting body.
The dormant, stress-resistant cell type that disperses and later germinates into a new amoeba.
The structural column of vacuolated, dead cells that holds the sorus aloft — an example of altruistic cell death.
The branching, head-to-tail chains amoebae form as they chemotax into an aggregation center.
The slug's directed movement toward light and warmth, guiding it to the soil surface for dispersal.
The feeding, dividing phase of single amoebae while bacterial food is available.
